definitions.explanation: The sour taste quality, one of the five basic tastes. Found in citrus fruits, vinegar, and fermented foods.

examples.japanese: このりんごは{酸味|さんみ}が{強|つよ}い。
examples.english: This apple has a strong sourness.

examples.japanese: レモンの{酸味|さんみ}が{料理|りょうり}を{引|ひ}き{立|た}てる。
examples.english: The acidity of lemon enhances the dish.

examples.japanese: {酸味|さんみ}と{甘味|あまみ}のバランスがいい。
examples.english: The balance between sourness and sweetness is good.

notes:
One of the five basic tastes. Refers to sourness or tartness as a flavor quality in food.

WORD FORMATION:
{酸|さん} (acid/sour) + {味|み} (taste)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {酸味|さんみ}が{強|つよ}い: strongly sour
- {酸味|さんみ}を{加|くわ}える: to add sourness
- {酸味|さんみ}が{利|き}いている: has a nice tangy flavor
- {酸味|さんみ}と{甘味|あまみ}のバランス: balance of sour and sweet

FIVE BASIC TASTES ({五味|ごみ}):
- {甘味|あまみ}: sweetness
- {酸味|さんみ}: sourness
- {塩味|しおあじ}/{塩気|しおけ}: saltiness
- {苦味|にがみ}: bitterness
- {旨味|うまみ}: umami (savory)

CONTRAST:
{酸味|さんみ} describes the taste quality. {酸|す}っぱい is the i-adjective meaning 'sour.'
